pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TUNE-UP

The parade is tomorrow. The band is in pieces.

The Clown Club is the band for the town parade, and every instrument they own was packed in one big red trunk.

Then Gwinn found the trunk.

Over it went. Keyboards, fiddles, horns and drums flew all over town, and they landed by family: one kind of instrument in each neighborhood. Doc Leo, the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, waits at the bandstand. He is not worried. He has Teddy.

Fetch each family home. Every time you do, the band plays one more part of the parade tune. Gwinn is very sorry. She is also having the best night of her life.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TUNEUP and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music, and it matters here: every neighborhood is scored with the instruments you are fetching. Without one, the PC speaker plays the notes.

Pick Read Storyline from the menu to see the story again, then pick Play. Thirteen neighborhoods wait, in order. After each one you land at the bandstand, a short stop where Teddy hands the instruments to the band and everybody plays what they have so far.

Instruments

An instrument to find wears a gold frame with a sparkle going round it. Walk into it and it is yours. Instruments in shop windows, or sitting on a stand, are just for looking.

The door out of a neighborhood opens when its whole family is found. Press F2 to see how many you are carrying, and F5 saves your game and F6 loads it. Look for the save sign on a bandstand.

Toy drummers march back and forth in some places. Hop over them, or wait for them to turn.

pages.head: Teddy
pages.html:
Teddy

A red-gold corgi with a white blaze, a ton of tricks, and a great nose for brass.

Left RightWalk.
UpHop. Hold it to hop higher. On a rope, a harp string or a cattail, Up climbs and Down lets you back down.
Q EHop up and to the left or right in one go.
DownSit.
SpaceBoop: paws up, nose to whatever is above. It plays piano keys, bells and drums, and it rings a staff door's hollow note.
FFetch what you are standing on.
F2Instruments carried.

Floating notes ring as you touch them. Touch one and it plays; a staircase of notes plays a scale if you climb it.

The rhythm neighborhoods

A few neighborhoods change the controls a little, and a card on the screen tells you when. At the roller rink Teddy skates by himself at the speed of the song: tap Up or Down to change lanes, and Left holds him back. On the marching field you play Doc Leo's baton instead: tap Up or Down to move it from line to line of the staff, and press Space as the note arrives. Nobody has to be quick. Every lit window is long enough for a slow hand, and the player piano keeps playing for anyone who needs more tries.

pages.head: Doc Leo and the Band
pages.html:
Doc Leo and the Band

Doc Leo is the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club: felt fedora, wire glasses, white paint round his eyes and mouth, and a sunburned nose. He waits at every bandstand, and so does the rest of the Clown Club, one clown to an instrument.

At a bandstand, walk Teddy up to the stand and the clowns take the instruments you carried, one each, and play them. The tune comes out a little fuller every time. By the end of the town it is the whole parade tune, and then the parade can begin.

Gwinn is somewhere in town, being sorry. She keeps turning up where the trunk landed.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

The families

The Piano Shop, the Player Pianokeyboards
The Music Store's Back Roomstrings
The Choir Loftvoices
The Basementbasses
The Arcadesynths
The Roller Rinkorgans and accordions
The Marching Fieldbrass
The Woods by the Riverwoodwinds
The Clock Towermallets and bells
The Farmpercussion
The Atticthe old stock instruments
Sound Checkthe drum kit

Every instrument is a picture of one of the music editor's presets, and it plays that preset's sound. If you open the editor's music tab afterward, you will know them all by sight.

Points

Each instrument found is worth 50 points. Floating notes, bells and the like score a little too.

pages.head: The Neighborhoods
pages.html:
The Neighborhoods

1. The Piano Shop

Hop the black-key ledges over the white keys and gather the keyboards. Each step on the shop's piano stairs plays a note.

2. The Player Piano

You are inside the piano. Notes drop down two glass tubes onto two keys. Stand under a key and press Space as its note lands. A row of notes across the top turns gold as the song plays; with 12 played, the door opens.

3. The Music Store's Back Room

Climb harp strings, bounce on springs that ring by pitch, and gather the strings.

4. The Choir Loft

A quiet climb. The voices come in one by one, and a chord blooms at the top.

5. The Basement

Low, dark rooms. Ride the speaker columns up in pulses on the beat, and follow the lamp that steps along with the click.

6. The Arcade

Neon tiles and wobbling pads. Pickups chirp in chords.

7. The Roller Rink

Teddy skates by himself. Change lanes with Up and Down to touch the notes of the tune.

8. The Marching Field

MEANWHILE... you play Doc Leo's baton. Notes glide along a staff; move the baton to their line and press Space.

pages.head: More Neighborhoods
pages.html:
More Neighborhoods

9. The Woods by the River

Doors made of staffs. Climb a cattail to the hollow note beside a door and press Space to play it; the door opens, and the tune is played walking through. Look closely at the reeds.

10. The Clock Tower

Curtains of tubular bells swing open when the clock hand reaches the gold wedge, so the clock is your countdown. Music-box gears turn. Mind the ticking up high.

11. The Farm

A cowbell on a cow, a woodblock at the woodpile, timpani like thunder. A hook lights its instrument for a moment; boop it from underneath while it is lit.

12. The Attic

The stock instruments are in an old trunk. Teddy plays Doc Leo's phrase on a toy piano to open it: two keys, then the latch.

13. Sound Check

Inside the bandstand's sound card, where the drum kit lives. The drum channels are doors, and two doors that share a channel take turns: snare and hi-hat, tom and cymbal. Wait for your door to open, then go.

When the last bandstand has the whole band, the parade can begin.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits and Registering

Tune-Up, version 1.0, November 1994. Design, art, music and programming by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic's AI model), made in code for Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition. Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs.

Starring Teddy as himself, Gwinn as herself, Doc Leo as the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, and the Clown Club as the parade band. The instruments are the pictures and sounds of the music editor's presets. No instruments were harmed. Gwinn would like that on the record.

This is shareware

Copy it for your friends and upload it to your favorite BBS. If you enjoy it, please register for $15 with Sandbox Software, Dept. TOOT TOOT, P.O. Box 000 (a made-up address: please don't mail anything). Registered players get a band roster poster, and our thanks.
